changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
changes.change: For retail buyers with stores and a website, especially store operations leaders, replace the claim with the walkthrough and their words: 'One system for the tills and the website.' Then show it step by step: an online order is returned at the till, refunded to the original payment, and recorded on one customer record, so it's 'one customer, one basket.' Drop 'unified commerce', 'in-person payments' and 'point of sale' in this context, and say 'the tills'.
changes.why: The head of store ops dismissed the M3 unified-commerce section as 'a diagram' and asked right away how a return works at the till, while the customer's own phrasing was 'One system for the tills and the website' and 'one customer, one basket'.

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For retail store rollouts, replace tiered support with single accountability and named people: 'One owner for your stores: we run the rollout and the installs under our name, with a named retail team that has done store rollouts.' Never present installs as 'a partner' handing off, because buyers have said 'I don't want two vendors pointing at each other.'
changes.why: The competitor reportedly brought 'people who'd done store rollouts', and our answer 'we'd bring in a partner' ended the store ops lead's questions because it failed the COO's stated criterion: 'I don't want two vendors pointing at each other.'

changes.change: Add a retail proof point set that sales can deploy on short notice: (1) a live demo of an online order being returned at a store till; (2) a sample store rollout plan covering dates, who installs, and what happens to the old tills; (3) reference retailers who will take a call quickly. Lead retail late-stage conversations with this proof instead of customer stories alone.
changes.why: The customer asked for three things: a reference call ('can I talk to them?'), a rollout plan ('Dates, who installs, what happens to the old tills'), and a live till return. We 'couldn't set up a call in time' and 'never showed' the return, while the competitor 'named retailers Angela knew'.

changes.change: Add an operations-led opener for retail deals with stores and a website, aimed at the COO and head of store operations as well as the CTO running the RFP. Start from the buy-online-return-in-store problem, where the store can't see the online order and loyalty breaks because store and web are 'two different customer records'. Lead with this before any checkout or wallet content.
changes.why: The evaluation was triggered by store returns and a loyalty program split across 'two different customer records', the deal was signed by the COO whom we met 'Once', and after the competitor's meeting the focus moved from web to 'it was stores'.
